title: Merchant ID Generation Verification
description: Verifies that the merchant is properly set up within the HSBC system and receives a Merchant ID. This is critical for onboarding and ensures only authorized merchants commence API integration. Automation: HIGH — validates response and DB artifact creation.
testDescription: A merchant representative requests onboarding on HSBC's UPI platform. The HSBC team verifies prerequisites and generates a unique Merchant ID, which is returned to the merchant and persisted.
prerequisites: HSBC UPI system is operational; Merchant has submitted onboarding request and documents; Backend supports ID generation; No prior Merchant ID exists for this merchant.
stepsToPerform: 1. Merchant logs in to onboarding portal. 2. Merchant fills out integration prerequisites (e.g., company/legal docs). 3. Merchant submits onboarding form. 4. HSBC verifies merchant details against internal database. 5. HSBC triggers Merchant ID generation workflow. 6. Merchant ID is generated and stored in HSBC system. 7. Merchant receives Merchant ID via secure channel/email. 8. Merchant logs into portal and verifies Merchant ID summary panel. 9. Merchant checks that no duplicate Merchant ID exists for their legal entity. 10. Audit log entry is created for Merchant ID creation event.
expectedResult: 1. Merchant ID is generated and visible to merchant in portal. 2. Merchant ID is persisted in HSBC onboarding database. 3. Merchant ID is unique — no duplicates for merchant entity. 4. Audit trail for Merchant ID creation exists.

sourceCitation.location: Page 1, Assumptions and Prerequisites
sourceCitation.excerpt: Merchant is setup on the HSBC system and Merchant ID is generated by HSBC

title: Encryption Key Assignment and Receipt
description: Validates HSBC's generation, secure delivery, and merchant receipt of the encryption key for API communication. Ensures secure symmetric key exchange fundamental for encrypted financial messaging. Automation: HIGH — pure API and system response checks.
testDescription: On onboarding, HSBC generates a symmetric encryption key specific to the merchant, securely delivers it, and the merchant verifies receipt and ability to decrypt handshake payloads.
prerequisites: Merchant ID has been correctly generated; HSBC encryption key generation function enabled; Secure communication channel exists; Merchant has key store ready for import.
stepsToPerform: 1. Merchant logs into integration portal. 2. Merchant submits key request via onboarding workflow. 3. HSBC generates unique symmetric encryption key. 4. HSBC transmits key via secure channel (e.g., portal download or encrypted email) to merchant. 5. Merchant downloads and imports key into application key store. 6. Merchant attempts to decrypt an HSBC-provided encrypted sample payload using the new key. 7. Merchant confirms decrypted message matches HSBC original. 8. Audit entry created for key generation and delivery. 9. HSBC logs successful key delivery event. 10. Merchant reviews log entry for secure key receipt.
expectedResult: 1. Merchant receives HSBC-generated encryption key. 2. Merchant successfully decrypts HSBC test message. 3. Audit logs confirm key generation and delivery. 4. Encryption key is not exposed in logs or audit records.

sourceCitation.location: Page 1, Assumptions and Prerequisites
sourceCitation.excerpt: Merchant Encryption Key is generated by HSBC and shared with the merchant

title: Merchant API Hosting Capability Validation
description: Ensures merchant's technical readiness to host, expose, and consume UPI APIs, including proper server configuration and endpoint availability. Safeguards integration reliability and establishes prerequisite compliance. Automation: MEDIUM — endpoint verifications and config checks.
testDescription: The merchant demonstrates hosting capability by deploying a test endpoint, exposing it, and validating accessibility and response to HSBC's test call. HSBC checks setup before granting production access.
prerequisites: Merchant has a server provisioned; Network/firewall allows API traffic; Merchant holds required certs/keys.
stepsToPerform: 1. Merchant logs into HSBC integration portal. 2. Merchant downloads API Integration Kit. 3. Merchant installs kit and sets up local endpoint. 4. Merchant configures API for HTTPS, port, and IP whitelisting. 5. Merchant exposes endpoint URL to HSBC. 6. HSBC sends a test request to merchant’s endpoint. 7. Merchant checks for correct request payload handling. 8. Merchant sends a test API call to HSBC’s endpoint and receives response. 9. HSBC verifies merchant endpoint responds within latency requirements. 10. HSBC confirms endpoint is reachable, TLS enabled.
expectedResult: 1. Merchant endpoint is accessible from HSBC and responds to test requests. 2. Merchant can consume HSBC APIs and receive valid responses. 3. HSBC confirms hosting capability preconditions met.

sourceCitation.location: Page 1, Assumptions and Prerequisites
sourceCitation.excerpt: Merchant has the capability to host and consume APIs

title: HTTPS/SSL Connectivity Enforcement
description: Validates that merchant–HSBC API connectivity strictly enforces HTTPS with SSL encryption for data in transit. Protects sensitive payment/PII data from interception or exposure. Automation: HIGH — protocol handshake checks.
testDescription: Merchant attempts to connect to HSBC UPI APIs using HTTPS/SSL, including submission of CSR and cert import. Non-HTTPS attempts are rejected, ensuring SSL-only communication.
prerequisites: Merchant possesses HSBC-issued digital certificate (cer file); Key store (jks or equivalent) configured; Public IP whitelisted.
stepsToPerform: 1. Merchant logs into portal. 2. Merchant generates CSR using Java keytool or equivalent. 3. Merchant uploads CSR to HSBC. 4. HSBC issues cer file and sends to merchant. 5. Merchant imports cer file into key store. 6. Merchant configures server for HTTPS/SSL on port 443. 7. Merchant attempts valid HTTPS handshake to HSBC API endpoint. 8. Merchant attempts plain HTTP connection to same endpoint (should fail). 9. Merchant submits API request over HTTPS and receives valid response. 10. HSBC logs SSL handshake event and certificate validation.
expectedResult: 1. HTTPS/SSL handshake to HSBC endpoint is successful, API request accepted. 2. Any plain HTTP/sans certificate attempts are rejected. 3. Certificate is validated by HSBC at connection. 4. Audit log records handshake and cert details.

sourceCitation.location: Page 1, Assumptions and Prerequisites
sourceCitation.excerpt: Merchant to connect with HSBC over HTTPS (SSL)

title: Dynamic VPA Validation Failure Path
description: Validates failure handling in Dynamic VPA Validation API when unknown or invalid subscriberId submitted, ensuring 'Failure' response and correct transMessage per specification. Protects from abuse and errors. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: Merchant submits Dynamic VPA Validation request with an invalid subscriberId. HSBC returns a Failure status with explicit error message, confirming that unknown records are appropriately rejected.
prerequisites: Merchant ID and key configured; Submitted subscriberId not present in HSBC database; API endpoint live.
stepsToPerform: 1. Merchant logs in to portal. 2. Merchant prepares Dynamic VPA Validation request with subscriberId=testsub999 (non-existent), source=SCB. 3. Merchant encrypts request and submits to HSBC API endpoint. 4. HSBC decrypts and attempts subscriberId lookup. 5. No matching record found, triggers failure branch. 6. HSBC responds with transStatus: Failure, transMessage: "Record not available for this Loan/Proposal No : testsub999". 7. accountDetails array is empty in response. 8. Merchant decrypts response and displays error. 9. Audit log entry is made for rejected validation. 10. Merchant checks logs for rejected event detail.
expectedResult: 1. API response contains transStatus: Failure and precise message. 2. accountDetails is empty. 3. Merchant logs event as validation failure. 4. No record or mapping is created in HSBC for invalid subscriberId.

expectedResult: 1. Minimum length (1 char) is accepted if valid, error for empty. 2. Over-max length is rejected with API-defined error. 3. Audit logs for field validation results.

testDescription: A merchant submits a Pre-Credit VPA Validation API request with a unique 'refNo', receives a successful response, then immediately re-submits with the identical 'refNo', verifying that the second attempt is flagged or ignored as a duplicate.

expectedResult: 1. First submission returns 'transStatus':'S' indicating successful processing. 2. Second and third submissions with same 'refNo' are rejected or flagged as duplicates, with 'transStatus':'F' or clear duplicity error in 'transMessage'. 3. No duplicate transaction is processed.

title: Partial Refund Handling (Amount Field Boundaries)

expectedResult:
